constraint_introduced: A path is simulated against the common ancestor of the open branches, never against the default branch. The viewer renders the result and computes no part of it. A runner merges each bundle onto its own integration branch and never onto the default branch.

findings.question: sensible
findings.text: The approach belongs in this repository and at this layer. ADR-0001 holds the viewer to one self-contained file under a content policy that blocks every external request, and the browser cannot run git. A path validated by a replay is therefore terminal work by construction, not by preference. Placing it in the pr plugin, next to the modes that already read git, follows the boundary the family already keeps.

findings.question: maintainability
findings.text: The approach helps. ADR-0020 records that viewer/index.html is the repository's largest maintenance problem, and it is decided and not executed. Every rejected option in intent.alternatives put its cost inside that file. This one leaves the viewer a render-only job, so the flightdeck does not enlarge the file before its own split has run. F5 is ordered last for the same reason.

findings.question: pattern
findings.text: New pattern, not a duplicate. ADR-0018 decided one derived record index that resolves every join between records, and it lists no pull-request-to-pull-request join. A path adds that relationship through a bundle rather than through a pairwise edge, which is consistent with how the index already reaches a pull request through its design.

findings.question: sensible
findings.text: The strongest finding, and it is about the baseline. Simulating against the default branch fails silently: it returns a well-formed, confident, inverted order. It did exactly that on the first run here. The constraint is now stated in ADR-0022's maps_to rule and carries an abort condition on this design, and it still rests on an implementer not reaching for HEAD because HEAD is what every other script in this repository reads.

findings.question: maintainability
findings.text: A risk the approach carries. ADR-0019 fixed the ledger vocabulary at comment, reply and state, and fold_threads skips a line it does not recognise. A path acceptance, a bundle merge and a blocked-pull-request decision are none of those three, so each needs its own projection. Three projections over one append-only file is the shape ADR-0019 intended, and nothing enforces that a future reader of the ledger handles all of them.

findings.question: sensible
findings.text: The integration-branch scheme is what makes accepting a path safe, and it is also the first remote write in this plugin family. Everything before it wrote into the bundle or the ledger. The runner is supplied by the adopting repository, so its credentials and its permissions sit outside this design, and no epic here can test them.

findings.question: maintainability
findings.text: The replay is a snapshot against recorded branch heads, and the projection it writes has no staleness marker. A reviewer opening the surface a day later sees a validated path with no indication that four of its branches moved. The publish manifest already solved a version of this with a content hash, and nothing in this design reuses that.

findings.question: sensible
findings.text: F1 duplicates the first epic of the inflight-record-store design, which already owns the open-pull-request entity gap. Building it twice is the likely failure. It belongs in shared code, and whichever design ships first should own it.

regret_risk: The design does work on the reviewer's behalf before they arrive, which is what makes it worth building and what makes it dangerous. A validated path is the first thing they read, and validation covers the merges, not the judgement. If the ordering is right more often than not, the team stops reading queues and starts reading one page, which is the whole point. If it is wrong even occasionally in a way the replay cannot catch, the surface will have taught them to accept an order they did not check, and the integration branches will make each wrong path cheap enough that nobody notices the pattern. Nothing in this design measures how often a proposed order is the one a reviewer would have chosen unaided, and the six done_when entries about presentation cannot substitute for that measurement.
